title: Small Edges 10mm - 90%
texts: 7 second hangs using a 10mm edge at 90% max effort

Completing training workouts on a smaller edge places a lot of stress on the soft tissue structures of fingers, finger joints and can be very skin intensive. For this reason, small edge training should only be used by climbers with a lot of training experience. 

The goal of this workout is to improve finger strength and to become accustomed to using a smaller hold size. Small edge training is useful to complete once you have followed a period of max hang training on a larger edge. This specific workout is a great way to increase maximum strength on smaller edges and can be used toward the end of a training phase to produce a peak performance.

This workout uses an edge size of approximately 10mm and an intensity of 90% max effort. You can either complete this session using 90% load found during small edge testing (described below) or using an RPE of 9/10. If using RPE each hang should feel like a 9/10 effort level, 10 being maximal effort/failure and 0 being no effort at all. As this is based on your perception of effort, the load used during this workout may change slightly between sessions. Please refer to the RPE scale if you are unsure. 

If using 90% of testing load please first complete a 'small edge testing session' on a 10mm edge under the Finger Strength category on the App.  This is calculated as 90% of your bodyweight + your score from the testing session. e.g. If you weigh 70kg and add 30kg in your maximal test, then your 90% intensity would be at 90kg total load or bodyweight plus 20kg of additional load in this example.


Complete the following 5 hangs using a fingerboard or edge that is skin friendly and around 10mm deep. Progressively build up the load during a warm up protocol until you are ready to train at the described workout intensity. It is also useful to warm up on bigger edges and reduce the edge size in the warm up until you reach the depth of hold used within this workout. You can increase the intensity of each hang by adding weight to your body or removing weight using the assistance of a. pulley system or theraband. Please make sure to keep the chosen intensity in mind and not go to maximal effort on each hang. 


Rate of perceived exertion (RPE)

RPE is a is a quantitative measure of a person’s perception of effort during sport and exercise. Crimpd uses RPE to determine the effort it takes to complete one set of given workouts. If a workout requires an RPE of 3, this equates to a perceived effort of 3 out of 10. 

10 – Maximal effort and often failure to complete more than one set of a workout at this intensity. 
9 – Close to maximal effort for each set of a workout. 
8 – High effort levels needed.
7 – Manageable but challenging, a reasonable high effort is required. 
6 – Moderate intensity with a moderate to high effort needed.
5 – Moderate effort required to complete each set.
4 – Low to moderate effort levels needed. 
3 – Very low effort levels. 
2 – Minimal effort needed
1 – Hardly any effort at all
0 – No effort
